Limitations
A document whose issuing country is not in the trust store gets the “Unknown issuer” verdict, not “Failed”. Importing a more recent Master List may fix this.
Revocation lists are not checked: they require network access, which Sceau never uses.
Terms of use
Reading assumes the holder presents their own document and consents.
The photo becomes biometric data under the GDPR if it is used for automated face comparison. Sceau does no such comparison and must not be used for it without a specific legal basis.
No data read is stored or sent: everything is wiped from memory when you leave the result or send the app to the background.

Sceau comes with no warranty. Its verdict covers the authenticity of the chip and of the data signed by the issuing state; it is not proof, and it does not tell whether the document has been reported lost or stolen.
Sceau is neither an official tool nor a certified identity verification service: it does not replace the identity checks that regulations require of certain professions.
